title: Call: Urgent Care Nurse — Dog Bite at the Fairgrounds

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - MCHD Nurse Manager Desk

transcript.speaker: NM
transcript.text: Marlow County Health Department, this is the Nurse Manager.

transcript.speaker: UC NURSE
transcript.text: Hi, this is Kendra Voss, I'm the charge nurse at Marlow Urgent Care in Fenwick. I've got an animal bite to call in, and, well, a question on top of it. Do you have a minute?

transcript.speaker: UC NURSE
transcript.text: Okay. Forty-six-year-old man, works maintenance at the Fairgrounds. Sunday afternoon, around 14:00 he thinks, he was hauling tables out of the Exhibition Hall after the supper, and a stray dog came in the side door and bit him on the right hand. Two punctures on the back of the hand, between the knuckles. Medium-size dog, brown, no collar. It ran off toward the livestock barns and nobody caught it.

transcript.speaker: UC NURSE
transcript.text: He didn't come in yesterday because it 'didn't look bad.' It's a little red today. We irrigated it, he's due for a tetanus booster so we gave one, and the provider's starting him on an antibiotic. Nobody has talked to him about rabies yet.

transcript.speaker: UC NURSE
transcript.text: So, who's handling the rabies side? Is that you, or do I call animal control directly? Nobody knows where the dog is.

transcript.speaker: UC NURSE
transcript.text: The other thing. He says he's had loose stools since about 07:00 this morning. Three or four times. No vomiting, he says no fever, temp here is 99.1. I heard on the radio about the Heritage Days supper. He was there working cleanup, he didn't have a ticket. I didn't ask what he ate. Do you want him on your outbreak list?

transcript.speaker: UC NURSE
transcript.text: Got it. He's still in room 2, but the provider wants to discharge him in about twenty minutes, so I'd like to tell him something before he walks out. Can somebody call me back at 555-0158 before noon?

voiceStyles.UC NURSE: Woman in her 30s, brisk and friendly, a busy clinic in the background, talking fast because a patient is waiting

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. The Nurse Manager should log the bite as routine and send it on for rabies risk assessment, a PEP decision and animal control. She should also screen the GI symptoms against the case definition. He worked cleanup, did not hold a ticket and has not yet been asked about food. She passes the Monday onset to the Epi Lead without pulling interviewers off priority cases. Onset arithmetic: Monday about 07:00 is roughly 36 to 38 hours after the 17:00–19:30 meal, so it falls inside the Salmonella window only if he ate supper food.
